title: Thai Red Curry with Tofu, Pumpkin and Coconut Milk
summary: A creamy vegan Thai-style red curry with tender pumpkin, golden tofu and fragrant coconut milk. It is warming, mildly spicy and perfect for a weeknight dinner with rice.

ingredients.name: pumpkin, peeled and cut into 2 cm cubes
curry powder, used as a Thai red curry paste substitute

steps: Pat the tofu dry with kitchen paper. Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a large pan over medium-high heat, add the tofu cubes and fry for 6–8 minutes, turning occasionally, until lightly golden on several sides. Remove to a plate.
Add the remaining 1 tbsp oil to the same pan. Add the onion and cook for 3–4 minutes until softened, then stir in the garlic, ginger and chilli for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the curry powder, paprika and ground coriander. Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly, so the spices bloom without burning.
Add the pumpkin cubes and stir to coat them in the spice mixture. Pour in the coconut milk and vegetable stock, then add the tamari, brown sugar and salt.
Bring to a gentle simmer, cover loosely and cook for 15–18 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the pumpkin is just tender when pierced with a knife.
Add the red bell pepper, green beans and fried tofu. Simmer uncovered for 6–8 minutes more, until the beans are bright green and tender-crisp and the sauce has thickened slightly.
Stir in the lime juice and basil leaves. Taste and adjust with a little more salt or lime juice if needed, then serve hot.
